record.paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: What is the generic-case complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?

evidence.quote: 6. What is the generic case complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a polycyclic group, given by a finite polycyclic presentation, so that every element of G has a unique normal form as a word in the polycyclic generators. The search conjugacy problem in G is the following algorithmic task: given as input a pair (u, v) of elements of G that are known to be conjugate in G, find an element x of G such that x^{-1} u x = v.

Recall the framework of generic-case complexity. For each n, let I_n denote the set of valid inputs (pairs of conjugate elements) whose total size (sum of normal-form lengths) is at most n, equipped with the uniform probability measure. A subset S of inputs is called generic if the fraction |S ∩ I_n| / |I_n| tends to 1 as n → ∞, and strongly generic if this convergence is exponentially fast. An algorithm A is said to solve the search conjugacy problem with generic-case complexity in a class C (e.g. polynomial time, linear time) if there exists a generic subset S of inputs such that A halts on every input in S within the resource bounds of C and outputs a correct conjugator, while on inputs outside S the algorithm may fail to terminate or output "don't know."

Determine the generic-case complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups: namely, identify the smallest natural complexity class C such that for every (or for a suitable broad family of) finitely presented polycyclic group G, there is an algorithm solving the search conjugacy problem in G with generic-case complexity in C, and prove a matching generic-case lower bound.
artifact.status_search_result: Related results exist: the uniform conjugacy problem over a family of polycyclic groups is known to be NP-complete (Cavallo–Kahrobaei, 2014), and generic-case polynomial-time algorithms have been established for related classes (e.g., Baumslag's group, free-by-cyclic groups). However, no source clearly settles the generic-case complexity of the search conjugacy problem in general polycyclic groups, so the status appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A family of polycyclic groups over which the uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs polycyclic groups whose uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete, addressing worst-case rather than generic-case complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Worst-case hardness is established but generic-case complexity is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Conjugacy in Baumslag's Group, Generic Case Complexity, and Division in Power Circuits
status_evidence.snippet: Generic-case polynomial-time results for conjugacy in Baumslag's group, illustrating the type of results sought but for a different group class.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous generic-case results exist for related groups, indicating the polycyclic case is studied but not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Generic-case complexity, decision problems in group theory and random walks
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper introducing generic-case complexity for group-theoretic decision problems.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework but does not settle the polycyclic search conjugacy case.
